name: And (King of Bashan)
title: The Giant King from Bashan
summary: Og was king of Bashan and the last survivor of the Rephaim, a people of giants. He was defeated by the Israelites under Moses' leadership, and his kingdom was given to half the tribe of Manasseh. He is known for his enormous iron bed, which was nine cubits long.

keyEvents.title: Battle against Israel at Edrei
keyEvents.description: Og went out with all his army to meet the Israelites in battle at Edrei, but the Lord gave him into Israel's hand.

keyEvents.title: God's promise of victory
keyEvents.description: The Lord told Moses not to fear Og, for God would give him and all his people and land into the hands of the Israelites.

keyEvents.title: Og's kingdom conquered
keyEvents.description: Israel captured sixty cities in Og's kingdom, all fortified cities with high walls, gates, and bars, as well as many unwalled villages.

keyEvents.title: The last of the Rephaim
keyEvents.description: And he is described as the last surviving Rephaim. His iron bed was nine cubits long and four cubits wide, and it was preserved in Rabbah among the Ammonites.

keyEvents.title: The Land Is Allotted to Manasseh
keyEvents.description: After the victory, Og's kingdom in Bashan was given to half of the tribe of Manasseh as their inheritance.

keyEvents.title: Remembrance of the Victory
keyEvents.description: The victory over Og is mentioned repeatedly in the Bible as an example of God's mighty deeds for Israel.
